name: Iowa
headline_status: Recreational marijuana is illegal in Iowa; a restrictive medical cannabidiol program allows registered patients non-flower THC products.
summary: Iowa's Medical Cannabidiol Program began with a 2014 low-THC oil law and was widened in 2017 and 2020; patients may buy up to 4.5 grams of THC every 90 days, but smokable flower and home growing are banned. Simple possession outside the program is still a jailable misdemeanor. In May 2026 Iowa doubled the number of medical dispensaries from five to ten and dropped the requirement that registered patients be permanent Iowa residents.

medical_since.value: 2014 (low-THC oil law), expanded to in-state production and sales by HB 524 (2017) and HF 2589 (2020).

possession_limit.value: Registered patients: up to 4.5 grams of THC per 90 days, unless their provider certifies more or they get a waiver. No legal amount for anyone else.

medical_program.value: A certifying practitioner (including physician assistants, podiatrists and advanced practice nurses since 2020) confirms a qualifying condition, such as chronic pain or PTSD. Only processed products are allowed, not raw flower.

retail_sales.value: Medical dispensaries only, supplied by two licensed manufacturers. HF 990 (signed May 2026) raises the dispensary cap from 5 to 10 and drops the requirement that registration-card holders be permanent Iowa residents; out-of-state cards still cannot be used at Iowa dispensaries.

penalties.value: First-offense possession of any amount can bring up to 6 months in jail and a $1,000 fine.

hemp_thc.value: Under HF 2605 (effective July 1, 2024), consumable hemp is capped at 4 mg THC per serving and 10 mg per container, and buyers must be 21+. A 2025 law bans open THC beverages in a moving vehicle's passenger area.

regulator.value: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services sets consumable hemp serving-size and labeling rules.

purchase_age.value: Medical only. Patients must be at least 18 to hold a medical cannabidiol registration card; younger patients are served through a primary caregiver.

public_use.value: There is no legal recreational use, and registered patients may not smoke medical cannabidiol; only processed forms are allowed.

dui.value: Zero tolerance: Iowa bans driving with any amount of a controlled substance in the blood or urine, which covers THC.

tourists.value: Limited. Out-of-state medical cards protect possession in Iowa but cannot be used to buy at Iowa dispensaries. HF 990 (2026) removed the requirement that Iowa card holders be permanent residents.

timeline.event: Law allows certain patients to possess low-THC cannabis oil
HB 524 creates in-state medical cannabidiol manufacturing and dispensing
Gov. Reynolds signs law replacing the 3% THC cap with 4.5 g of THC per 90 days and adding PTSD
HF 2605 hemp potency caps and 21+ age limit take effect
HF 990 signed, doubling medical dispensaries to 10 and dropping the Iowa residency requirement for patient cards

faq.a: No. Recreational marijuana is illegal, and even a first possession offense can mean up to 6 months in jail. Only registered patients may buy limited medical cannabis products.

faq.q: Can you smoke medical marijuana in Iowa?
faq.a: No. Iowa's program allows processed products only, not raw flower.

faq.q: How much THC can Iowa medical patients buy?
faq.a: Up to 4.5 grams of THC every 90 days, unless a provider certifies more or the patient obtains a waiver.

faq.q: Are THC drinks legal in Iowa?
faq.a: Hemp-derived THC products are legal for adults 21+ if they stay within 4 mg per serving and 10 mg per container.
